hypotheses.KAMA: Adaptive smoothing may reduce whipsaw from noisy hedging flows while retaining persistent repricing; not established edge in these assets.
hypotheses.ENSEMBLE: Different repricing horizons may favor a diversified trend vote; volatility clustering motivates reduced exposure, not return prediction.
hypotheses.ROTATE: Gold and silver react differently to monetary and industrial demand; relative persistence may justify buffered rotation, but only two correlated assets limits diversification.

ENSEMBLE.schedule: first available session of ISO week

ROTATE.incumbent: signal-model state from full prior history, does not imply preexisting position at segment restart

volatility: sample std log EUR close returns *sqrt252, nonpositive/nonfinite ->weight0
execution: previous completed close features; next scheduled open; integer shares floor(weight*opening equity/open); sell before buy; affordability includes costs; GLD/PHAU before SLV/PHAG tie/order; no leverage/short; no stops between rebalances; terminal close liquidation modeled with same costs
currency: USD proxy converted with strictly previous available ECB USD/EUR, <=7calendar days; EUR ETC direct; lagged FX approximation not actual FX executions

costs.basis: model fixed SMART EU schedule; excludes tax, data subscription; not actual executed fees

sensitivity: all family lookbacks jointly rounded(scale*lookback); KAMA fast2 fixed; targetvol.10 and rotationbuffer.02 fixed; not one-at-a-time full sensitivity
